audits.title: Identification and Management of Hyperprolactinaemia in Patients With Intellectual Disabilities Who Are Prescribed Antipsychotic Medication: A Retrospective Audit
audits.standard: Prolactin measured in the last 12 months for patients on antipsychotics and elevated results managed per current guidelines
audits.setting: Richmond and Kingston intellectual disability psychiatry caseloads

cycle1.result: 39 (52.0%) had prolactin measured in the last 12 months; 16 (41.0%) of these were elevated; 81.3% of elevated results discussed and treatment considered.

audits.other_findings: 68.8% of those with raised prolactin were on risperidone; uptake of blood tests is the main issue.
audits.citation: Healy S, Patel R. Identification and Management of Hyperprolactinaemia in Patients With Intellectual Disabilities Who Are Prescribed Antipsychotic Medication: A Retrospective Audit. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S235-S235. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.574.

audits.title: Audit on prolactin monitoring for patients on oral risperidone, intramuscular risperidone, and intramuscular paliperidone
audits.standard: BNF: prolactin monitoring at baseline, after 6 months and then annually
audits.setting: Community and inpatient services in Torfaen, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board

cycle1.result: 23 of 28 patients on risperidone never had prolactin measured; only 2 of 28 had appropriate monitoring in 2018.

audits.intervention: Highlighting baseline prolactin monitoring and adding baseline prolactin to admission bloods for psychosis or antipsychotic use
audits.other_findings: 150 patients' clinic letters were screened; a full audit of metabolic monitoring on antipsychotics was suggested.
audits.citation: Bader M. Audit on prolactin monitoring for patients on oral risperidone, intramuscular risperidone, and intramuscular paliperidone. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S65-S65.

audits.title: Hyperprolactinaemia: audit of practice and new guidance
audits.standard: Locally agreed audit standards (95%) on frequency of prolactin monitoring, time to review and referral
audits.setting: Enfield South Locality Team, Barnet, Enfield and Haringey Mental Health Trust

cycle1.result: Only 7/30 (23.33%) tested within the last year; no audit standards met. 2 (6.667%) had new hyperprolactinaemia, both reviewed and treated within one month.

audits.intervention: New risk-stratified hyperprolactinaemia guidance developed (awaiting ratification).
audits.other_findings: Reasons for failure included loss to follow-up, tests not requested and missed appointments. Re-audit planned for 2020.
audits.citation: Janaway B, Anwar L. Hyperprolactinaemia: audit of practice and new guidance. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S196-S197.

audits.title: An Audit on the Monitoring and Management of Hyperprolactinemia in Inpatient Adults on Regular Antipsychotics in 8 Acute Wards in an NHS Mental Health Trust
audits.standard: NICE and local guidance on prolactin monitoring and management of hyperprolactinaemia
audits.setting: 8 acute adult inpatient wards, Nottingham Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Of 41 on regular antipsychotics, 19 had no prolactin assay during admission; 44.4% of antipsychotic-naive patients had baseline prolactin; hyperprolactinaemia in 9; 9.1% with hyperprolactinaemia had symptoms assessed; 27.3% had actions taken

audits.other_findings: 78 records screened. Need to raise clinician awareness of prolactin monitoring.
audits.citation: Zhang P, Li Z. An Audit on the Monitoring and Management of Hyperprolactinemia in Inpatient Adults on Regular Antipsychotics in 8 Acute Wards in an NHS Mental Health Trust. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S13-S13.

audits.title: Audit of Prolactin Levels Monitoring for Inpatients on Antipsychotics in SABP
audits.standard: NICE and Maudsley guidance: baseline prolactin before antipsychotics with medium or high hyperprolactinaemia risk
audits.setting: 9 inpatient wards, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Baseline prolactin checked in 33 patients, compliance 43%

audits.other_findings: 3 had raised prolactin; symptoms of hyperprolactinaemia were not documented for any of them. 127 case notes reviewed.
audits.citation: Majid Z, Fulmali A, Tamilson B, Bloxam R, Varma D, Abdallah L, et al.. Audit of Prolactin Levels Monitoring for Inpatients on Antipsychotics in SABP. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S165-S165.

audits.title: Prolactin Monitoring for Inpatients on Antipsychotic Drugs: A Clinical Audit
audits.standard: NICE: prolactin checked 6 months after starting then every 12 months, with enquiry about symptoms (not required for aripiprazole, clozapine, quetiapine, olanzapine under 20 mg)
audits.setting: Adult inpatients of a general psychiatric hospital

cycle1.result: Prolactin measured in 80.6% (25/31) in last year; 48% (12/25) hyperprolactinaemic, with action in 5 (41.7%); of 9 on drugs needing monitoring for a year, 8 (88.9%) measured, 5 elevated, action in 3 (60%).

audits.other_findings: Hyperprolactinaemia in 58.3% of women and 38.5% of men; 25.8% on two antipsychotics.
audits.citation: Kotait F, Parmar S, Kar N. Prolactin Monitoring for Inpatients on Antipsychotic Drugs: A Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S243-S244. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.592.

audits.title: Prolactin Monitoring in Antipsychotic Prescribing: A Trust-Wide Completion of Audit Cycle
audits.standard: NICE and Maudsley guidelines for baseline and follow-up prolactin monitoring with medium- to high-risk antipsychotics
audits.setting: Working-age and old-age psychiatric inpatient wards, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Prolactin monitoring compliance 47% for patients established on antipsychotics before admission and 43% for inpatient initiation.

cycle2.result: Prolactin monitoring compliance 100% both before admission and at inpatient initiation; of 25 started on medium- to high-risk antipsychotics, 9 had hyperprolactinaemia, 4 had appropriate management and 3 had repeat testing.

audits.other_findings: Trust-wide recommendations from the 2021 audit were implemented but not described. Management of raised prolactin remains poor; a standardised pathway with electronic prompts and education is proposed.
audits.citation: Kim A, Emambocus A, Wiggins T, Moon S, Hammond T. Prolactin Monitoring in Antipsychotic Prescribing: A Trust-Wide Completion of Audit Cycle. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S313-S314. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11676.

audits.title: Adherence to Prolactin Monitoring Guidelines in Children and Adolescents Prescribed Risperidone: A Clinical Audit From a Tertiary Mental Health Service in the United Arab Emirates
audits.standard: Local hospital guidelines aligned with NICE CG155: prolactin at baseline, 12 weeks and six months after starting risperidone
audits.setting: Behavioural Sciences Institute, Al Ain Hospital, tertiary child and adolescent mental health service

cycle1.period: Data collected April–July 2025 (patients started from January 2023)
cycle1.result: Prolactin at 12 weeks documented in 12%, with reasons for non-monitoring in 8%; baseline and six-month monitoring more often completed (figures not given).

audits.other_findings: 86% of patients were male and 96% had psychosis with neurodevelopmental conditions. Electronic reminders, staff education and better documentation were recommended.
audits.citation: Alazeezi S, Ahmed Z, Ali D, Javaid S. Adherence to Prolactin Monitoring Guidelines in Children and Adolescents Prescribed Risperidone: A Clinical Audit From a Tertiary Mental Health Service in the United Arab Emirates. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S306-S306. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11691.

audits.title: Serum Prolactin Level Monitoring in Children and Adolescents on Antipsychotic Treatment: Evaluating the Current Practice in Al Ain, United Arab Emirates
audits.standard: NICE CG155: prolactin at baseline, 12 weeks and every six months in children on antipsychotics
audits.setting: Child psychiatry outpatient clinic, Al Ain Hospital

cycle1.result: No baseline prolactin measured; 10 (7%) checked at 12 weeks; none checked six-monthly

audits.other_findings: Local guidance, staff training and electronic monitoring alerts recommended, with re-audit after one year.
audits.citation: Javaid S, Afzal A, Ahmed Z. Serum Prolactin Level Monitoring in Children and Adolescents on Antipsychotic Treatment: Evaluating the Current Practice in Al Ain, United Arab Emirates. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S135-S135.

audits.title: Monitoring of prolactin levels in children and adolescents prescribed antipsychotic medication: a complete audit cycle.
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on monitoring and managing hyperprolactinaemia with antipsychotics
audits.setting: Beechpark Autism Service (child and adolescent), Dublin

cycle1.result: Baseline serum prolactin 28.6%; six-monthly repeat prolactin 28.6%; management of hyperprolactinaemia 0%.

audits.intervention: Recommended guidelines and changes implemented (details not stated).

cycle2.result: Baseline prolactin 57%; six-monthly repeat prolactin 39.1%; management of hyperprolactinaemia 12.5%.

audits.other_findings: Management of hyperprolactinaemia improved only minimally.
audits.citation: Uduehi E, Gallagher L, Alugo T. Monitoring of prolactin levels in children and adolescents prescribed antipsychotic medication: a complete audit cycle. Ir J Psychol Med. 2017;34(1):45-51. doi:10.1017/ipm.2016.14. PMID: 30115169.
